comment.body:
Thanks for the PowerToys.Settings.exe Event Viewer entry and PowerToysReport_2024-07-26-09-01-11.zip. The event establishes the 0.82.1 Settings crash with code 0xc000027b, but KERNELBASE.dll alone does not identify the originating UI operation. A focused scan of the supplied Settings text logs did not establish that originating exception, so please do not resend the same ZIP or event.

Please provide:
1. The shortest numbered sequence that triggers the crash: does Settings fail before any page opens, when opening a particular page, or after changing one specific control? Name that page/control and whether the crash happens every time.
2. Whether the same sequence still fails on the latest stable PowerToys, including the tested version shown in About (or the executable's Properties > Details if Settings cannot stay open).

This selects the startup or page-initialization path for a targeted maintainer investigation rather than treating KERNELBASE.dll as the root cause.

actions.label: Approve Settings exception-localization plan
actions.note: Red-confidence investigation candidate, not a proven behavioral fix; preserve the originating exception before changing error handling.

judgment.rationale: The supplied event and archive establish a Settings failure, but the triggering operation and actionable originating exception are still missing.
evidence: The report includes a Settings 0.82.1 crash event with exception 0xc000027b and Windows kernel version 19041.
A focused in-memory text scan of the supplied archive did not identify an originating XAML/unhandled/stowed-exception message; this is not crash-dump analysis.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the exact Settings operation and current-build confirmation, then localize the original exception before proposing a behavioral repair.

fix_assessment.rationale: A Settings UI exception-localization and subsequent targeted error-path correction is applicable, but no root-cause-specific fix or linked implementation was found. The candidate deliberately does not claim that an unrelated logged warning caused the crash.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve the originating Settings UI exception and correct its failing operation
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a Settings startup/navigation UI operation raises a WinRT stowed exception that escapes without enough operation context to identify the underlying failure. The event's 0xc000027b is consistent with this boundary, but does not identify a resource, dependency or page as the cause.
plan: Use the reporter's exact operation on a matching Windows test environment and a current build, breaking on the originating exception rather than the final KERNELBASE event.

Trace the matching Settings app startup/navigation handler and existing unhandled-exception logging; preserve the original exception/HRESULT and current page/operation through that boundary without swallowing arbitrary UI exceptions.
Only after localization, repair the demonstrated resource, lifetime or operation precondition at its owner; do not treat optional missing-tool warnings or a generic catch-all as a crash fix.
Add a regression for the exact failing operation and an exception-context logging check that avoids personal paths/settings values.
verification: The original numbered sequence no longer crashes on the affected Windows/build combination.
A fault-injected equivalent preserves the originating error and operation context; normal startup and unrelated Settings pages remain functional.

confidence.rationale: The event establishes a stowed-exception boundary, not its origin; no operation-specific repair can yet be justified.

issue_context.summary: Settings 0.82.1 crashes with a Windows Application Error entry naming KERNELBASE.dll and code 0xc000027b. The author subsequently supplied the requested diagnostic archive, but no triggering page/action is described.
known_information: The report supplies the faulting Settings executable version and exception code.
PowerToysReport_2024-07-26-09-01-11.zip is already public in the author's comment.
Live issue is open, unassigned and labeled Product-Settings/Severity-Medium.
The archive's Settings logs contain optional-tool/settings warnings, but none was correlated to the reported terminal crash.
inferences: KERNELBASE.dll is the recorded exception boundary, not evidence of a Windows kernel defect.
A WinUI operation failure is plausible; the responsible page, resource or dependency remains unknown.
issue_context.analysis: A second blanket ZIP/Event Viewer request would ignore evidence already supplied. Request the minimal action sequence and current-build result, then use the archive and an operation-specific debugger trace to identify a real fix.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report and both comments; enumerated cross-reference #39027 without treating title similarity as a proven duplicate.
Inspected the already supplied ZIP in memory, enumerated Settings text logs and scanned for originating XAML/unhandled/stowed-exception text; did not perform dump or binary event-log analysis.
Did not equate informational missing-pwsh warnings with the terminal crash.
No fixing PR appeared in the reviewed timeline or direct issue-number PR search.
